title: Teaching in his senior years and hopes for an opera
summary: At 78 he prefers to stay teaching rather than tour, comments on Eubie Blake, and asks DeMichael to help find a sponsor for his opera.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yes, sir. That's my influence. I put God first and then after that, then I have to take all the rest of them. You know, one time I had a mind to doing an act like this, when I would go out there and started singing and I'd sing a part of it and I'd tell Louis to come in and you do your part, Louis. Then I'd sing like Louis, and I'd -- I would say, hey, now, look out, Randy, now you take this one. Then I would start to singing, you know, one of those things. Well, I don't know. I get to thinking, well, here I'm here, teaching. I better just stay on here, teaching, instead of getting out here on the road. And I'd get my sleep now, where I can get my rest. Got in the senior years, I'm 78. So it would be best to cool it, don't you think?
I guess so. I know Eubie
Blake's still going. Eubie's 93 now, I think.

Well, I don't know. I get to thinking, I just want to put some talent out there now, try to see if I can get some people doing some things. Get them to do things that I want them to do. Try to get them to do the things I want them to do. And I want to get this opera going, if I can.

I'm going to try to keep in touch with you because I want to keep you informed about this opera, because I want to -- you probably can help me to get a sponsor or an agent or something. If you find out what the opera is going to be like.
